It makes the sentence a yes/no question: are you a teacher?

revised.prompt: Mia has three weeks and 30 minutes a day before a work trip to Jakarta. She needs small talk, directions and reading short emails. Which plan best meets these criteria?

options.label: Drill common sentence patterns, key affixes and daily dialogues, reading aloud
Learn every prefix and suffix rule exhaustively, skipping vocabulary until each rule is fully mastered
Study formal grammar tables only, leaving all conversation practice until she arrives in Jakarta
Memorise a 1,000-word alphabetical list, postponing grammar and speaking practice until the last week

revised.prompt: A learner often writes 清 when she means 请 (as in 请问). Which analysis uses the structure of the characters correctly?

options.label: 青 is the radical in both, and 讠 and 氵 are only stroke variants of the same component
请 has the speech radical 讠, 清 has the water radical 氵, and both use 青 as a sound hint
请 has the water radical 氵 and 清 has the speech radical 讠, with 青 as the shared meaning part in both
The two share the radical 讠 and differ only in tone, so the reader must use context to tell them apart

revised.prompt: You prepare a reading text for intermediate learners. Criteria: train reading from context as in real newspapers, yet prevent misreading of words that context cannot settle. Which diacritics policy fits best?

options.label: Leave the text unvowelled except on ambiguous words, where a short vowel or shadda is added.
Remove diacritics from the whole text, ambiguous words included, to match the look of authentic newspapers.
Vowel the final case endings on most words, since internal vowels can usually be guessed from the root.
Vowel each word fully in the first half of the text, then drop all diacritics for the second half.
